xs = torch.linspace(-3, 5, 400)
h1 = torch.relu(xs + 1.5)
h2 = torch.relu(xs - 0.5)
h3 = torch.relu(xs - 2.5)
bump = h1 - 2 * h2 + h3
1. Combine three shifted hinges into a compact bump.

Follow the pieces: before the first hinge, all units are silent and the output is zero.
After the first breakpoint, $h_1$ starts the climb. The coefficient $-2$ on $h_2$
reverses the slope at the peak, and $h_3$ cancels that downward slope at the final
breakpoint. Four linear pieces $\rightarrow$ one compact bump.
computedVariants: The peak g(0.5) = 2 and the four piece slopes 0, +1, -1, 0 are computed by the player and by the tests from the declared breakpoints and coefficients (the slope on piece k is the sum of the first k coefficients; the peak is the sum at the middle breakpoint). The chapter says the bump 'peaks at the middle breakpoint', 'returns to zero' and has 'four linear pieces' (fig-alt L259, prose L272-275) but prints neither the value 2 nor the slopes. The picture writes the peak as a bare numeral at the apex; the sentence g(0.5) = 2 is carried by the SVG title, the live aria-label and the transcript.

The finished bump is drawn as a pale green target silhouette from the first frame, before it is constructed: the declared bump evaluated at the same 161 samples, filled over [-1.5, 2.5] with a light dashed edge over the same span. It is a target to aim at, not a second measurement, which is why it is the same green as the running sum, and it is retired only once the sum equals it at every sample.

The running sum is drawn as h1 first; then one eased amount (2 s, easeInOutCubic) both swings the drawn middle ramp from +h2 down to -2 h2 and admits h2 into the sum from coefficient 0 to -2, so the ramp turning over and the sum folding are one motion seen twice; then h3's amount eases 0 to 1. Those entry amounts are drawing devices of this scene's timeline -- a reveal, not a control -- no intermediate value of either is ever written on the picture, and no intermediate sum is a number of the chapter.

The curves are drawn through 161 samples on the domain, -3 + 8 i / 160, chosen so the three breakpoints are sample points and every piece is drawn straight; the chapter's figure samples 400 points. Each ramp is drawn only from its own breakpoint rightwards, since it is zero before it. The y-range of the plot, -1.1 to 3.1, clips the ramps and the folding sum where they leave it; the chapter's left panel shows them whole.

The slope entries, the peak numeral and the bracket on [-1.5, 2.5] are drawing devices of this scene, not numbers of the chapter: at most two slopes of the four stand at any instant, each written against the piece it measures and each the slope of the running sum on that piece at that moment.

The formula line g(x) = h1 - 2 h2 + h3 is the chapter's `bump = h1 - 2 * h2 + h3` written with the book's \predictionpart and \featurepart macros; the chapter's figure legend writes it as $y = h_1 - 2h_2 + h_3$ (L268).

Each valve is a small learned layer squashed by a sigmoid
a number in $(0,1)$ read as *what fraction passes*
The LSTM cell as a conveyor belt with valves.
The upper additive route is the long-memory highway.

computedVariants: THE VALVE OPENINGS ARE DECLARED ILLUSTRATIVE, NOT MEASURED. Chapter 10 prints no gate value anywhere near @eq-lstm: the equations define f, i, o as sigmoid layers and stop. This scene therefore declares three openings -- 1.0, 0.5 and 0.0 -- and stands each valve only at one of them: the forget valve goes 1.0 -> 0.5, the write valve 0.0 -> 1.0, the read valve 0.0 -> 0.5 -> 0.0. The union of the values the three valves take is exactly that declared set, which a test asserts. The panel, the intro, the caption-bearing boundary paragraph and the picture itself (a small note reading 'illustrative openings') all say so. A valve is interpolated between two of these stops only while it is visibly turning.

The carried numbers c_{t-1} = 1.00 and the candidate c~_t = 0.50 are round numbers chosen to be read off the picture, not measurements and not a chapter fixture; the chapter prints neither. Real states are vectors, and this scene draws one unit of them.

c_t = f (*) c_{t-1} + i (*) c~_t and h_t = o (*) tanh(c_t) -- @eq-lstm's last two lines -- are recomputed by the player and, independently, by scripts/test_lstm_valves_excerpt.cjs at every scrubbed time from the published openings. At the declared stops this gives c_t = 1.00, then 0.50 after the forget valve closes halfway, then 1.00 again after the write valve admits the candidate; and h_t = 0.00, then 0.38 = 0.5 * tanh(1.00) when the read valve opens halfway, then 0.00 when it shuts. The chapter prints none of these.

The answer the scene exists for is a recomputation, not an assertion: with o = 0 the equation gives h_t = 0 for every c_t, while c_t = f c_{t-1} + i c~_t does not contain o at all, so the cell state is bit-for-bit what it was before the valve shut. The tests assert both halves at every time, and separately that with f = 0 the old content is gone while i (*) c~_t still writes (c_t = 0.50), by re-declaring the forget valve's stops on a fresh panel.

The chapter's two MEASURED mean forget-gate activations, about 0.76 for the task-solving model and about 0.56 for the default-initialized one (the fig-forget-gate-diagnostic caption, sixty-four probe sequences, eighty steps, one seed each), are quoted in the boundary paragraph as that experiment's measurement and nowhere else. They are never given to a valve, never drawn on the picture, and never raised to a power; a test asserts neither string ever appears inside the pane at any time. The scene's read-valve trajectory deliberately avoids printing 0.76: tanh(1.00) = 0.76 is an intermediate the picture does not number, because a 0.76 on this picture would be mistaken for that measurement.

The picture's devices are this scene's, not the chapter's: the carried value drawn as a bar whose height is its number; the bar sliding along the belt and taking whatever the belt holds where it stands (c_{t-1} before the forget valve, f c_{t-1} between it and the sum, c_t after); the dashed ghost left at the inlet, and the dashed ghost of the hidden state's open height, each drawn only where it clears the bar it is a ghost of; the word 'unchanged' beside the cell state once the read valve has shut; and the valve itself as a port with a vane lying along the flow when open and across it when shut. The film (6050-Ch10 SLSTMDesign) draws a rotating vane whose angle is the opening; this panel keeps the vane and fixes its mapping so that open is along the flow.

The film's own valve values -- 0.86, 0.78, 0.72 -- are schematic and are NOT imported. Nor is its gold 'additive cell-state highway' colour, its 'INHERITED FROM CHAPTER 9'S SKIP ROUTE' banner, its purple/blue/green per-valve palette or its two equation cards: the book's palette puts every carried value in \featurepart blue, leaves the valves in the emphasis ink because nothing here is learned by the reader's hand, and spends its one orange on the tag saying the weight matrices behind the valves are learned.
